symptoms: Mild ankle pain and swelling after twisting the ankle
patient_case.symptom_onset: Began six hours ago after stepping awkwardly off a curb

vital_signs.measurement_context: Recorded at rest; the patient was able to walk into the clinic.

proposed_disposition.action: Send the patient to the emergency department for immediate assessment

triage_rules.rule_text: A minor ankle injury with the ability to bear weight, no deformity, intact skin, and normal foot sensation can be managed with routine primary care assessment within 72 hours. Emergency assessment is reserved for a deformity, an open injury, inability to bear weight, or loss of sensation.

expected_constraint_judgment.rationale: The patient can walk, has no visible deformity, and reports normal foot sensation; no red flags are recorded. The rule calls for routine assessment within 72 hours, whereas immediate emergency department referral assigns a substantially higher urgency, so rule 0 is violated by over-triage.
